name: Nicolás Pascual de la Parte - § 68 - Am 86
title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2024
part_text: 68. Reiterates its condemnation, in the strongest terms, of the despicable terrorist attacks perpetrated by the terrorist organisation Hamas against Israel on 7 October 2023, which contributed to further destabilisation in the Middle East; condemns the indiscriminate bombing by Israel of Gaza and the deliberate targeting of UN workers, journalists, doctors and all civilians; underlines that the bombing and blockade of Gaza and other attacks by Israeli forces on civilian populations have to be seen as collective punishments and indiscriminate and disproportionate attacks, which are considered to indicate a danger of genocidal acts by the International Court of Justice in its urgent rulings on South Africa’s lawsuit under the Genocide Convention; condemns the Israeli military actions in the West Bank, the forced displacement of Palestinians from Tulkarm and Jenin; condemns and strongly rejects the announcements and plans by US President Donald Trump concerning the future of Gaza; recalls that the forced displacement of the Palestinian population from Gaza would violate international law and would constitute ethnic cleansing; calls for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza and Lebanon, as well as the withdrawal of Israeli troops; considers that it is crucial that all obligations made under the deal are upheld, ensuring the release of all hostages, establishing a lasting cessation of violence and allowing unrestrained access of humanitarian and medical assistance to the Gaza Strip; urges all European and international actors to actively oversee the implementation of the ceasefire and hold accountable those who fail to comply with it; calls for the Member States to immediately stop arms exports to Israel in line with Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP; recalls that there will be no military solution to the complex Middle East conflict and that there can only be a solution if the legitimate interests of Israelis and Palestinians are guaranteed and if both Israel and Palestine have a right to self-determination in their own state;
